title: Self-powered UV sensing with perovskite/polymer nanocomposites
summary: A materials-to-device study using fluorescent CsPbBr3@Cs4PbBr6/PU nanocomposites in a triboelectric nanogenerator for self-powered UV sensing.
question: How can a functional nanocomposite translate a light stimulus into a useful sensing response without an external power source?

workflow.title: Material development
workflow.text: Prepared the perovskite/polymer nanocomposite and worked through the material-processing challenges needed to obtain a stable system.

workflow.title: Characterisation
workflow.text: Used structural and spectroscopic characterisation to verify the material and study the response relevant to the device.

workflow.title: Device translation
workflow.text: Integrated the material into a triboelectric nanogenerator and evaluated its use for self-powered UV sensing.

workflow.title: Research communication
workflow.text: The work was developed into a first-author publication and presented through scientific conferences and symposiums.

outcome: The project connected chemistry, materials characterisation and device behaviour in one research workflow rather than treating them as separate tasks.
reflection: The most useful part of this work was learning to follow a material from synthesis and verification through to a functioning device, then explain why the measured behaviour mattered.

publication.title: Fluorescent CsPbBr3@Cs4PbBr6/PU polymer nanocomposite-based triboelectric nanogenerator for self-powered UV sensing

institution: CSIR-Central Food Technological Research Institute (CFTRI), Mysuru
title: Optimizing Curcumin Yield from Turmeric Oleoresin
summary: A four-week chemistry internship investigating curcumin extraction and purification from turmeric powder and curcumin-removed turmeric oleoresin.
question: How could extraction and purification conditions be compared to improve curcumin yield or purity in turmeric-derived materials?

workflow.title: Extraction
workflow.text: Worked with turmeric powder from market and farmer sources using cold percolation, and also compared a Soxhlet extraction route described in the internship work.

workflow.title: Purification
workflow.text: Used hexane washing and compared IPA, IPA:hexane (1:1.5) and MTBE during curcumin purification from oleoresin.

workflow.title: Characterisation
workflow.text: Used UV-Vis results to quantify curcumin content and worked with FTIR and HPLC data for comparison of purified samples; TLC and 1H NMR were also used in the CRTO part of the study.

workflow.title: CRTO study
workflow.text: Applied a choline chloride:propylene glycol deep-eutectic-solvent approach to curcumin-removed turmeric oleoresin, followed by centrifugation, filtration and spectroscopic/chromatographic checks.

workflow.title: Comparison
workflow.text: Compared yield and purity across extraction and purification conditions. The report found IPA produced high UV-Vis purity values, while FTIR and HPLC comparisons supported IPA:hexane as the strongest purification condition among the tested solvents.

outcome: The internship compared multiple extraction and purification routes rather than claiming a new process. In the report, the farmer and market oleoresins initially contained 16.48% and 14.62% curcumin by UV-Vis, and the CRTO study increased the reported UV-Vis curcumin content from 10.41% to 13.15%.
reflection: This project gave me practical exposure to natural-product extraction, purification, instrumental analysis and the trade-off between yield, purity, solvent choice and sustainability in a short research internship.

institution: Maharani's Science College for Women, Mysuru
title: A Survey on PCOS in Mysore City
summary: A questionnaire-based cross-sectional B.Sc. project exploring self-reported PCOS occurrence and related lifestyle or symptom patterns among 104 respondents in Mysuru.
question: To study PCOS occurrence among women surveyed in Mysuru and examine how reported symptoms and lifestyle factors varied across respondents.

workflow.title: Questionnaire design
workflow.text: Prepared a Google Forms questionnaire covering reported PCOS status, age, BMI, activity, diet, sleep, stress, menstrual issues and other symptoms; the report states that the questionnaire was designed with guidance from a senior gynaecologist.

workflow.title: Data collection
workflow.text: Collected 104 responses between December 2021 and January 2022. Names and email addresses were not collected in the survey described in the report.

workflow.title: Descriptive analysis
workflow.text: Organised the responses by age group and compared reported PCOS status with lifestyle and symptom variables using tables, percentages and charts.

workflow.title: Result
workflow.text: Eleven of the 104 respondents reported PCOS. The report then examined how those responses were distributed across age groups and other self-reported factors.

workflow.title: Interpretation and limits
workflow.text: The project was an exploratory academic survey based on a convenience sample and self-reported information, so its results should not be treated as a representative estimate for the whole city or as evidence of causation.

outcome: The project produced a 104-response dataset and a descriptive analysis of self-reported PCOS status, symptoms and lifestyle variables. It was a B.Sc. academic survey, not a clinical or diagnostic study.
reflection: This was an early research project that introduced me to study design, participant data, descriptive analysis and the importance of interpreting survey results within the limits of the sampling method.

title: Halide Perovskites: From Chemistry to Reproducible Data Analysis
summary: A 28-day guided foundation project using a real JARVIS halide-perovskite dataset to connect chemistry, materials concepts and reproducible Python analysis.
question: How do PBE and HSE band gaps compare across halide perovskites, and how are electronic properties related to tolerance-factor and stability descriptors?

workflow.title: Chemistry foundation
workflow.text: Revisit atomic structure, ions, electron configuration and the A, B and X sites in ABX₃ halide perovskites so every variable is interpreted chemically rather than treated as a column name.

workflow.title: Reproducible data inspection
workflow.text: Use Python with JARVIS tools, pandas and NumPy to load the dataset, inspect its shape and columns, document selected descriptors and mark uncertain interpretations for verification.

workflow.title: Structure–property analysis
workflow.text: Build publication-quality plots and examine relationships among computed electronic properties, tolerance-factor or stability descriptors and band-gap behaviour without treating correlation as causation.

workflow.title: Baseline modelling
workflow.text: Introduce a simple linear-regression baseline only after the exploratory analysis, including a transparent comparison of PBE and HSE band gaps and basic model evaluation.

workflow.title: Scientific communication
workflow.text: Turn the analysis into a reproducible notebook, figures, a short research note and a GitHub-ready README that state assumptions, limitations and what the results do not prove.

outcome: The intended outcome is a reproducible materials-analysis workflow, not a claim of new material discovery.
reflection: This project is designed to close the gap between learning Python and applying it to a chemically meaningful materials problem. Computational values, correlations and a simple regression will be reported with their limitations.
